sources.title: Good Riddance (Time of Your Life)
sources.notes: Studied for reusable acoustic-strumming behavior only. Main guitar: GM program 24, 2048 notes, 684 exact onset groups, mostly 0.25/0.50-beat attack gaps, common 2-5-note attacks, and most 4/4 bars around 11-12 audible attacks on a sixteenth grid. User identified the rendered character as a useful common warm acoustic-strumming reference. Exact source rhythm, pitches and harmony are not stored in Materials.

sources.title: A Horse with No Name
sources.notes: Studied for rolling triplet acoustic-strumming behavior. Type-0 MIDI at 192 ticks per beat and 125 BPM. Main steel-string channel used GM program 25 and contained 3074 note-ons. Grouping adjacent note-ons within 12 ticks produced about 1015 strum groups with a median width of 3 notes. Attacks aligned overwhelmingly to beat starts and late-triplet positions. Beat-start groups with recoverable direction were strongly low-to-high, while late-triplet groups were almost entirely high-to-low. Within-stroke spread had a median around 20 ms and 90th percentile around 47.5 ms. Exact harmony, pitches and full source rhythm are not stored in Materials.

sources.title: Torn
sources.notes: Studied first as supporting evidence for warm-pop steel-string strumming, then separately for a more general pop-rock bass behavior. The bass used GM program 33 and contained 735 attacks. About 83% of adjacent attacks repeated the same pitch; 0.50- and 0.25-beat attack gaps dominated; many bars used about 9-10 attacks; bass attack positions strongly overlapped the main accompaniment rhythm while exact kick coincidence was much lower. This source motivated the normal-pop-rock-bass Material. Exact bass pitches, chord progression and full rhythmic masks remain source-specific.

sources.title: You Were Meant for Me
sources.notes: Studied for gentle steel-string strum-picking behavior. The MIDI is type 1 at 384 ticks per beat and about 111 BPM. Two long-running guitar channels used GM program 25. Channel 0 contained 490 note-ons from roughly beat 8 to 461 with median velocity about 72; channel 6 contained 896 note-ons from roughly beat 10 to 460 with median velocity about 55. After grouping close onsets, one channel was dominated by single-note attacks while the other mixed many single notes with many three-note partial groups. Common adjacent gaps were approximately 1/3, 2/3 and 1 beat. This source motivated the gentle-steel-strum-picking Material. Exact pitches, harmony and full rhythm remain source-specific.

sources.title: Zombie
sources.notes: Current promoted studies cover Muted Guitar, section-linked bass, the continuous overdriven rhythm track, and the separate sustained melodic Overdriven Guitar track. The Muted Guitar track contained 440 note attacks forming 224 onset groups, used GM program 28, had a median nominal gate around 0.41 beat, and contained no CC64 sustain events; it therefore supports a genuinely clipped muted pulse interpretation. Two separate GM program 29 Overdriven Guitar tracks must not be conflated. The sustained melodic Overdriven Guitar track contained 157 note attacks forming 103 onset groups, used sparse single notes and dyads, had median onset-group duration around 1.49 beats, and contained no CC64 sustain events; this track motivated sustained-overdrive-guitar. The separate rhythm Overdriven Guitar track contained 766 note attacks forming 388 onset groups, with 374 two-note groups and 384 adjacent onset gaps exactly one beat. Its raw MIDI note gate had a median around 0.38 beat, but the same track contained 96 CC64 sustain events forming 48 pedal-down blocks, each about 7.99 beats long. Therefore its audible role is not a series of isolated short stabs: it is repeated re-articulation over a continuously sustained overdrive bed. This corrected interpretation replaces the earlier short-gate overdrive abstraction and now motivates continuous-overdrive-rhythm-bed. The bass track contained 745 attacks and showed a strong section-role link: muted-guitar bars overwhelmingly paired with a sparse 1-2-4 bass mask and long beat-2 sustain, while sections with the continuous overdrive rhythm track overwhelmingly paired with a fuller 1-2-3-4 bass pulse and high attack alignment. The separate chorused clean track remains unpromoted for later study. Exact pitches, chord progression, full rhythmic sequences, controller sequence and arrangement remain source-specific.

sources.title: Smooth Operator
sources.notes: Studied for flowing melodic-support bass behavior. The bass channel used GM program 35 and contained 516 completed notes over MIDI 26-48, with no CC64 sustain and no pitch-wheel events. Median duration was about 0.70 beat, median onset spacing 1.0 beat, and median note-off-to-next-note-on gap about 0.22 beat. Common onset gaps were 0.5 beat (217), 1.5 beats (164), and 1.0 beat (58). About 36.1% of adjacent notes repeated pitch, about 25.2% moved by one or two semitones excluding repeats, and about 95.7% stayed within five semitones. This source motivated smooth-melodic-support-bass and supports the broader bass-line-continuity Skill. Exact melody, harmony and full rhythmic sequence remain source-specific.

sources.title: Give Me the Night
sources.notes: Studied for groove-motif melodic bass behavior. The dedicated SYNTH BASS track used GM program 38 and contained 730 completed notes over MIDI 24-55, with no CC64 sustain and no pitch-wheel events. Median duration was about 0.22 beat, median onset spacing 0.5 beat, and median note-off-to-next-note-on gap about 0.28 beat. Common onset gaps were 0.5 beat (312), 0.25 beat (169), 0.75 beat (92), 1.0 beat (52), and 2.0 beats (46). About 11.2% of adjacent notes repeated pitch, about 49.2% moved by one or two semitones excluding repeats, and about 66.5% stayed within five semitones. Exactly one-octave moves occurred 111 times, with 79 upward and 32 downward. Velocity was comparatively stable at 98-110 with median 101. This source motivated groove-motif-bass and supports the broader bass-line-continuity Skill. Exact melody, harmony and full rhythmic sequence remain source-specific.
